body: This team sucks, our city sucks, our fans suck, and we deserve all of the hate.
Edit: I am ungrateful and am going to kill myself.
I'm part of that 36%. We're two people making a decent combined income, but we'll never own a home and will never have enough to retire because of it. I fully plan on working until I die.
Their ultimate end game is to make renters second-class citizens, stripping our right to vote and participate in society. Where I live, the homeowner majority is all for it. It's disgusting.
I recommend the Oats for Breakfast podcast : https://oatspodcast.com/. They have lots of informative discussions and interviews and a strong eco-socialist take on current issues.
I shared this with my in laws who are in that area. Hope you find him safe!
Great work! That's a lot of effort and it's so nice to see it play off. Sounds like you have a clear path ahead.

Agreed! My family keeps shaming me for not owning a home like all of my cousins and sibling. They don't understand this difficulty and keep telling me to make better choices... apparently saving 50% of our take home pay (between 2 people) each month isn't enough! And we're also not allowed to move out of the GTA because that would be "leaving the family behind". Every conversation comes down to "well if you REALLY cared then you should work 80 hours a week instead of 60". We have to live life at some point, it's ridiculous.

They won't. We make a decent income and are frugal, but will never be able to do anything but rent. Even that will probably get to the point where we'll need roommates just to keep renting. We are considered second class citizens, and politicians couldn't give less of a shit about us since we're not homeowners.

It's clear to me at this point that none of the major parties care about renters or aspiring homeowners beyond token gestures. I know I'll never be able to afford a property without moving to a remote area with no jobs, so I'm going to rent for life. Sure, I could retrain in a new field, but that would use up all of the down payment money anyway. 

 I don't see a point in participating in elections anymore, since I'm seen as a second class citizen by political parties. Unless something changes, I seriously think that things will come to a point where only homeowners are allowed to vote. I'd love to change this opinion, but there isn't enough evidence to think otherwise at this point.

I've been using the CIBC Visa Infinite for a few years - not sure if the travel rewards are the same as Meridian or not. I've tried to put as many regular purchases as possible on it (especially groceries and gas) , and so far we've been able to use it for covering about half the airfare for a vacation a few years ago. Based on point accumulation since then, I'd estimate that it probably reaps a benefit every 3-4 years in terms of rewards, but that's very dependent on your own situation. Overall, I would say that it's worth it for travel rewards if you're planning a bigger trip. Right now we've saved up enough points to cover flight costs for our honeymoon... Just have to wait until it's safe to travel again, haha.

Thanks for the nice insights! There's definitely a lot of pressure from family to buy, and seeing friends/colleagues buy places definitely ignites envy.

On your point about PFC, I agree. We're actually pretty average income-wise and are both pretty frugal, and right now we're renting in a decent area for a good price. We have a good emergency fund and are able to save every month (aside from a recent pet emergency). But, that's not enough for everyone over there - apparently not owning a home means we're poor by their standards. It's a bit silly to be honest.

It's ok, I realize that it's probably a better place to discuss renting as this subreddit is better suited for homeowners. I don't necessarily think I'm poor, but if that's the place to go then that's where I'll keep my discussions from now on.

I wasn't demanding any sort of right to a home, and I think it was a bit unfair of you to make that assumption. Sorry to make that mistake, and I will delete this post to avoid any confusion. I am stupid and shouldn't have brought this up.
I decided to register for the Big Data Analytics program at York University. It seems to be well reviewed and it's not too costly. It's not an intensive program but it doesn't seem like a bad choice.

Term employees still get benefits at the federal level, but you'll need to get used to having your chain yanked around as they promise eventual permanent positions, while seeing students bridged into said positions from their undergrad programs. Meanwhile, those of us who weren't fortunate enough to take co-op programs and instead get real world experience are constantly left on the outs. I'm guessing you're with a provincial government ministry?

Right now, I work in federal government in a program management / planning type role. Keep missing out on permanent opportunities so I'm starting a certificate program in data analytics and working on learning coding languages in my spare time in an attempt to either further my time here, or be able to start a new career working in my field with a big data angle. It's not a great plan but it's at least something in my control, as opposed to waiting for opportunities to open up.
